verses.text: Then Joshua called together the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
He said to them, "You have done everything Moses, the servant of the LORD, commanded you, and you have obeyed me in everything I told you.
For a long time now, right up to today, you have not abandoned your fellow Israelites. You have carefully done the work the LORD your God gave you.
Now the LORD your God has given your brothers rest, as he promised. So go back home to your own land, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you east of the Jordan.

But be very careful to obey the commands and the law Moses gave you: love the LORD your God, live the way he wants, obey his commands, hold on to him tightly, and serve him with all your heart and all your soul."
Then Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went home.
Moses had given land in Bashan to one half of the tribe of Manasseh, and Joshua had given the other half land west of the Jordan with their relatives. When Joshua sent them home, he blessed them
and said, "Go back home with your great wealth: large herds of animals, silver, gold, bronze, iron and lots of clothing. Share with your relatives what you took from your enemies."

So the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh left the rest of Israel at Shiloh in Canaan to go back to Gilead, their own land, which they had received as the LORD commanded through Moses.
When they came to Geliloth near the Jordan, still in the land of Canaan, they built a large, impressive altar there by the river.
The other Israelites heard people say, "Look, the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar at the border of Canaan, near the Jordan, on the Israelite side."
When the Israelites heard this, the whole community gathered at Shiloh to go to war against them.
So the Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead.
With him they sent ten leaders, one for each tribe of Israel. Each one was head of a family group among the clans of Israel.
They went to the people of Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead and said to them,
"The whole community of the LORD says: How could you be so unfaithful to the God of Israel? How could you turn away from the LORD today and build yourselves an altar, rebelling against him?
Was the sin at Peor not enough for us? To this day we have not been cleansed from it, even though a plague struck the LORD's people.
And now you are turning away from the LORD! If you rebel against the LORD today, tomorrow he will be angry with the whole community of Israel.

If the land you own is unclean, come over to the LORD's land, where the LORD's tent stands, and share our land with us. But do not rebel against the LORD or against us by building another altar besides the altar of the LORD our God.
Remember Achan son of Zerah. He was unfaithful about the things set apart for destruction, and God's anger fell on the whole community of Israel. He was not the only one who died for his sin."
Then the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the heads of the clans of Israel,
"The Mighty One, God, the LORD! The Mighty One, God, the LORD! He knows, and let Israel know too! If we did this in rebellion or unfaithfulness to the LORD, do not spare us today.
If we built this altar to turn away from the LORD, or to offer burnt offerings, grain offerings or peace offerings on it, may the LORD himself punish us.
No! We did it because we were worried. We feared that one day your children might say to our children, 'What do you have to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?
The LORD has made the Jordan a border between us and you people of Reuben and Gad. You have no share in the LORD.' Then your children might cause our children to stop worshipping the LORD.
So we said, 'Let us build an altar, not for burnt offerings or sacrifices,

but as a witness between us and you and the generations after us. It will show that we too worship the LORD in his presence with our burnt offerings, sacrifices and peace offerings.' Then in the future your children will not be able to say to ours, 'You have no share in the LORD.'

We said, 'If they ever say this to us or to our children, we will answer: Look at this copy of the LORD's altar, which our ancestors built. It is not for burnt offerings or sacrifices. It is a witness between us and you.'

We would never rebel against the LORD or turn away from him today by building another altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings or sacrifices, besides the altar of the LORD our God that stands in front of his tent."
When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the community, the heads of the clans of Israel, heard what the people of Reuben, Gad and Manasseh said, they were pleased.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to them, "Today we know that the LORD is with us, because you have not been unfaithful to him in this. Now you have saved the Israelites from the LORD's punishment."
Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders left the people of Reuben and Gad in Gilead and went back to the Israelites in Canaan and told them what had happened.
The Israelites were glad to hear it, and they praised God. They spoke no more about going to war against them to destroy the land where the people of Reuben and Gad lived.
And the people of Reuben and Gad named the altar Witness, saying, "It is a witness between us that the LORD is God."
